lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Independent application: recognising pressure tactics and scams

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic recognising pressure tactics and scams task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner reads four short fictional messages (a text, an email, and two phone-call summaries) written for this lesson, decides which are legitimate and which are scams, and names the specific tactic used in each scam message.
safetyNotes: All four messages are fictional and written for this lesson; no real phone numbers, links, or company names are used.
If the learner has actually received a message like one of these, remind them not to click any link or reply, and to show a trusted adult the real message separately from this lesson.
materials: learner-local: the four provided fictional messages

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Name one thing you could do before reacting to any message like these, that doesn't depend on already knowing it's a scam.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u04-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Legitimate-vs-scam classification: Classifies three of the four messages correctly. | Naming the specific tactic: Names a real tactic (urgency, unearned reward, refusal to identify, unnecessary information request) for each scam message and quotes supporting text. | Transfer to a general response: Names a concrete pause-before-reacting step that works regardless of whether the message turns out to be real. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write one new fictional scam message of their own using a tactic not covered in the original four (for example, pretending to be someone they know), then trade the reasoning with a sibling, parent, or trusted adult who tries to name the tactic without being told.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic recognising pressure tactics and scams task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: recognising pressure tactics and scams worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner reads four short fictional messages (a text, an email, and two phone-call summaries) written for this lesson, decides which are legitimate and which are scams, and names the specific tactic used in each scam message.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact recognising pressure tactics and scams decision or action.
Model move 2: Before reading the four messages, write down what you already think makes a message feel like a scam.
Model move 3: Read each of the four fictional messages and decide whether it is legitimate or a scam.

Model check: Legitimate-vs-scam classification: Classifies three of the four messages correctly. | Naming the specific tactic: Names a real tactic (urgency, unearned reward, refusal to identify, unnecessary information request) for each scam message and quotes supporting text. | Transfer to a general response: Names a concrete pause-before-reacting step that works regardless of whether the message turns out to be real.

resources.title: recognising pressure tactics and scams action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for recognising pressure tactics and scams.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: recognising pressure tactics and scams coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner reads four short fictional messages (a text, an email, and two phone-call summaries) written for this lesson, decides which are legitimate and which are scams, and names the specific tactic used in each scam message.
Coach direction: Before reading the four messages, write down what you already think makes a message feel like a scam.
Learner prompt: In your own words, what is one sign that has made you suspicious of a message before, real or imagined?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: recognising pressure tactics and scams complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Read each of the four fictional messages and decide whether it is legitimate or a scam.
Response 1 (t2-p1): Message 1 (a text saying a prize was won and asks to confirm a card number to claim it): legitimate or scam?
Response 2 (t2-p2): Message 2 (an email from a school reminding about a schedule with no links or requests): legitimate or scam?
Response 3 (t2-p3): Message 3 (a call summary claiming an urgent problem that must be fixed in the next ten minutes or there will be serious consequences): legitimate or scam?
Response 4 (t2-p4): Message 4 (a call summary from a caller who will not say which company they represent but asks to 'verify your identity' first): legitimate or scam?
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: recognising pressure tactics and scams minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Name one thing you could do before reacting to any message like these, that doesn't depend on already knowing it's a scam.

Success checks: Legitimate-vs-scam classification: Classifies three of the four messages correctly. | Naming the specific tactic: Names a real tactic (urgency, unearned reward, refusal to identify, unnecessary information request) for each scam message and quotes supporting text. | Transfer to a general response: Names a concrete pause-before-reacting step that works regardless of whether the message turns out to be real.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: recognising pressure tactics and scams supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g10-u04-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional recognising pressure tactics and scams condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Legitimate-vs-scam classification: Classifies three of the four messages correctly. | Naming the specific tactic: Names a real tactic (urgency, unearned reward, refusal to identify, unnecessary information request) for each scam message and quotes supporting text. | Transfer to a general response: Names a concrete pause-before-reacting step that works regardless of whether the message turns out to be real..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
